answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so renewing fails the primary objective; deferring creates a hard 14-day lapse with the line already at 94% and no buffer, which spikes delivery risk. The plan is a guarded switch: memory_c2 is the load‑bearing case (low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit-cost cuts last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing), and memory_c1 is the counterweight I'm verifying so I correctly price the stability I'm giving up across a hand-off. memory_c6 is retained as background context — multi-year volume pricing with the incumbent is no longer reachable this cycle because they won't reopen. Verification of c2 confirms onboarding fits inside the 14-day window (or I escalate to defer); verification of c1 confirms the migration cost and contingency value of staying with the incumbent during transition. Single-decision constraint is respected: the move itself is the action, with second-source backup staged but not executed this cycle unless c2 verification reveals onboarding risk incompatible with the deadline.
